# Independent audit: true-Minkowski-centroid paired tails

Audited all four sections of `candidate af4e7610828e864b`. **PASS.** The source verifier `supporting computation verify_minkowski_centroid_paired_tail_obstruction_two_sided.py` was independently rerun: **246 exact checks pass**. This note audits an auxiliary counterexample and its two corrected inequalities; it does not claim OC.

## 1. Actual bodies, sum, centroid, and cuts

The cone-strip body has section length x on [ell(w),h(w)]. Hence its area is 1/2 and its centroid is w/2+1/(6w^3). The midpoint sum really is the cone strip on the averaged support interval: for any admissible total x coordinate one can choose two admissible summand x coordinates, and the interval sum is exactly the full vertical interval of that total length. Thus both inclusions hold, not merely a volume identity.

Direct integration gives m=(u+v)^2/(8uv) and g=(u+v)(3u^2v^2+1)/(12u^2v^2). Subtracting the two separate centroids gives exactly the displayed negative offset. The rational counterexample uses an actual supporting edge in A and a strictly proper cap in B. The support-edge mass is zero in planar area, and both displayed positive distances of the B cut were checked. The positive rational deficit (6) is therefore a genuine upper bound on the paired infimum below the proposed lower bound.

## 2. Uniform small-parameter scope and orders

For 0<s<=1/100, u=1+s+2s^2 and v=1+s satisfy 1<v<u<51/50. The function h(w)-mu(w)=1/(2w)-1/(6w^3) is decreasing. Therefore tau_old>=2mu(v)-h(v)>=1/3. Also tau_old<mu(v)<1<=h(v). The true-centroid displacement is Dg=s^4(u+v)/(3u^3v^3)<s^4, and ell(v)<=s. Consequently tau>=1/3-2s^4>s>=ell(v), while tau<h(v). All cuts used in the polynomial identity thus have their asserted statuses uniformly, including along the rational sequence s down to zero.

The exact rational identities in (7), their denominators, and all ten positive coefficients of P are correct. Dividing by m-a gives (8), whose lower bound tends to infinity along rational s. Since P(A,B;g_M) is no larger than the displayed paired cap, this falsifies every finite linear excess payment. The same positive denominator bounds give a divergent ratio to (m-a)^alpha for every alpha>3/4. No claim at alpha=3/4 follows. Moving from the average centroid to the true centroid increases the chosen paired mass, with the stated exact positive difference; the obstruction survives that correction. Opposite translations preserve M and merely shift the free scalar tilt, as asserted.

## 3. Residual-BM replacement

If U+V<a, both residual cuts have positive volume. Their actual midpoint is contained in the opposite closed halfspace through g_M. Its volume is at most (1-Gamma_d)m, because the other centroid halfspace has mass at least Gamma_d m and the common hyperplane is null. Brunn--Minkowski gives (10).

For residual volumes x,y in [0,a] with x+y=a+q, concavity of the root gives x^(1/d)+y^(1/d)>=a^(1/d)+q^(1/d), including d=1. The quantity being raised to the dth power on rearrangement is nonnegative: m>=a and 1-Gamma_d>=1/2 imply 2[(1-Gamma_d)m]^(1/d)>=a^(1/d). This proves the positive-part formula (9). If U+V>=a the right side is at most a, so the omitted case is immediate. The d=1 interval equality and the stated planar constant at m=a are both correct.

## 4. Shape-error replacement and existence

The volume-normalized homothet K has actual volume a and centroid g_M. For each fixed opposite translation, the loss against K in any halfspace is at most the missing volume, namely half the symmetric difference because the two bodies have equal volume. Applying the previously proved ordinary paired-centroid-tail theorem to K and summing the two losses proves (12) after minimizing the displayed actual shape error. The ordinary dependency and its existing independent audit were read; this step does not use OC or a two-body compensation lemma.

Translation is continuous in L1 for bounded convex bodies. Outside a sufficiently large ball, both translated bodies are disjoint from K, and the error is the constant 2a. Thus the minimum is attained either inside a compact ball or at any point in that exterior constant region. No unattained selector, boundary-mass substitution, or uncontrolled shape-to-volume estimate is involved.

## 5. Separate elementary width observation

For an equal-volume planar pair, write w_A,w_B for the widths in one normal direction and h_A,h_B for the upper supports. The actual Minkowski centroid obeys 2u.g_M<=h_A+h_B-(w_A+w_B)/3 by the ordinary centroid support-width bound. For paired thresholds alpha,beta with alpha+beta=2u.g_M, a cap contains a homothetic copy of its body scaled by its relative distance below the upper support, provided that distance lies in [0,1]. If a threshold lies below the lower support, its cap already has area a. Otherwise put p_A=max(0,(h_A-alpha)/w_A), and similarly p_B. These numbers lie in [0,1], satisfy w_A p_A+w_B p_B>=(w_A+w_B)/3, and give U+V>=a(p_A^2+p_B^2). In particular U+V>=a/9. The stronger Cauchy bound is

    U+V >= a(w_A+w_B)^2/[9(w_A^2+w_B^2)].

This observation is valid for every actual pair of closed halfspaces. It will be used in the separately audited middle-superbody result if its complete source is saved; no all-dimensional extension is inferred here.
